summary: H.R. 1755, titled the 'Timely and Accurate Benefits Act,' requires states to use an Enhanced Income Verification Platform within one year of the Act's enactment in order to remain eligible for federal funds for covered federal benefit programs.

affected_groups.effect: Must procure, contract, and use an Enhanced Income Verification Platform within one year to remain eligible for federal benefit program funds.
Subject to automated, real-time verification of a wide range of income sources and deposit account transaction data, with the option to review and attest to the data's accuracy.
affected_groups.group: Applicants and recipients of federal benefit programs

key_provisions: States must procure, contract, and use an Enhanced Income Verification Platform within one year of enactment to receive federal funds for covered benefit programs.
Applies to any federal, state, or local program where benefit eligibility or amounts are determined by individual or household income.

Defines 'enhanced gross income' to include wages, contract and gig work, unemployment, Social Security, SSI, interest, rental income, royalties, child support, cash assistance, regular gifts, trust distributions, and other taxable or non-taxable income.
Requires platforms to use automated, real-time data matching and analytics to find unreported income, inconsistent reporting, or potential ineligibility and improper payments.

Requires platforms to analyze consumer-permissioned deposit account transactional data to verify income sources not found in existing tax or payroll data, while allowing claimants to review and attest to data accuracy.
Requires platforms to identify and consolidate overlapping data to prevent double-counting of financial records.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 1755, titled the 'Timely and Accurate Benefits Act,' requires states to use an Enhanced Income Verification Platform within one year of the Act's enactment in order to remain eligible for federal funds for covered federal benefit programs.
summary_detail.significance: The bill mandates a standardized technological approach for verifying income across federal benefit programs administered by states, tying the receipt of federal funds to the adoption of enhanced data-matching platforms.
